title: Does 3D Gen Studio even work?
author: NooneLikesYouBill
selftext:
First off, been working on this 8+ hours a day and now on my fourth day. My brain is mush and I am really at my frustration limit. Doing my best to keep my cool. (I've reformat 5x since starting all this, including 2x already today, I am at my limit)

3.5.3, nothing works 

Tried pointing to existing Comfy install - fails - every single node is missing.

Tried doing the managed Comfy install - fails - I turn on the auto launch option, doesn't do anything.

Using Kanban mode, try doing a Image Edit (2nd panel) - fails - dev console says "Failed to run..  something" going from memory because I'm reformatting a 3rd fucking time.

(leaving 100+GB of models and shit in %appdata%, not good for people with ocd)

I don't even know what to do at this point. ChatGPT and Gemini Argon got nowhere (easily 200 screenshots trying to diagnose between the pair, total fail).

Just very frustrated.

comments.author: cheyumaama
comments.body: What are you trying to do? Generate 3D assets?

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: I have never used that , the easiers thing if you have windows at least just install the comfyui windows app, find the trellis and other templates in comfyui , go to them , they will throw errors for models missing and download them, you have to move them I think. Or just use the blender mcp for now, and have whatever agent drive that. 3D generative models are ok but still lacking, you might get better or acceptable results with just the mcp servers

comments.author: sunnystormy64
comments.body: Bro... you don't \*need\* ComfyUI, just the Python sandbox to run the models. Codex can help you with that.

comments.author: Haman24
comments.body:
Honestly, I've been there with local AI art tools. The constant reformatting, missing nodes, and troubleshooting just to get a working install is the absolute worst. It sounds like you're dealing with infrastructure problems, not a creative problem.

When I just need 3D models for a project, I skip the local setup now. Been using Rapid Assets as a cloud based alternative. It just works, no wrestling with dependencies or leaving gigs of junk in appdata. The 3D gen is solid for quick assets, but I mostly stick to their 2D to 3D workflow with a reference image because I get more predictable results. What kind of assets are you trying to make for your project?
